questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Is triangle ABC congruent to triangle DEF? If so, give a rigid motion that carries ABC onto DEF. If not, explain why.
questions.prompt_markup: Is triangle ABC congruent to triangle DEF? If so, give a rigid motion that carries ABC onto DEF. If not, explain why.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. The reflection across the y-axis carries A to D, B to E, and C to F.
questions.grading_note: Any valid rigid motion or sequence. The conclusion and a motion that works are both required.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Is triangle ABC congruent to triangle PQR? If so, give a rigid motion that carries one onto the other. If not, explain why.
questions.prompt_markup: Is triangle ABC congruent to triangle PQR? If so, give a rigid motion that carries one onto the other. If not, explain why.
questions.correct_answer: No. ABC has legs 3 and 4, but PQR has legs 3 and 5. A rigid motion keeps every length, so none can carry one onto the other.
questions.grading_note: Form required: "No" with a length (or area) that differs. Areas 6 and 7.5 also show it.

sections.skill: Decide congruence for figures given by measurements, including curved figures

branch.new_demand: Decide congruence when figures are given by measurements (or are curved), justifying with a motion or an invariant.

questions.skill: Decide congruence for figures given by measurements, including curved figures
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Circle P has radius 3 and circle Q has radius 3. Explain, using a rigid motion, why they are congruent.
questions.prompt_markup: Circle P has radius 3 and circle Q has radius 3. Explain, using a rigid motion, why they are congruent.
questions.correct_answer: Translate P's center to Q's center. Every point 3 units from P's center goes to a point 3 units from Q's center, so circle P lands on circle Q.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation using a translation that matches the centers.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Sector P has radius 4 and central angle 50°. Sector Q has radius 4 and central angle 50°, drawn in another place and turned. Are they congruent? Explain with a rigid motion.
questions.prompt_markup: Sector P has radius 4 and central angle 50°. Sector Q has radius 4 and central angle 50°, drawn in another place and turned. Are they congruent? Explain with a rigid motion.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Translate P's center onto Q's center, rotate so one bounding radius of P lies along one of Q's, and reflect across it if the arcs are on opposite sides. Equal radii and equal 50° angles make the arcs match.
questions.grading_note: Any valid motion with a reason using the equal radius and equal angle.
